panels.figure_caption: A section of this lesion composed of uniform round-shaped cells with indistinct cells and rounded sharply pinched out nucleus with amphophilic to eosinophilic cytoplasm. The nuclei of the cell are centrally located and have homogenous chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli, no mitoses seen. The background of the lesion shows a prominent vascular component. Histopathology finding: glomangioma.
in_text_mentions: Gross histopathological analysis revealed a single small well-circumscribed bluish papule originating from the right-sided chest wall. Microscopic examination showed a circumscribed mass with an abundance of vasculature components consisting of dilated capillaries that are lined by endothelial cells surrounded by multiple layers of glomus cells (Figures 2-4). A glomangioma diagnosis was made.

in_text_mentions: was made to proceed with excisional biopsy through a small incision. The patient was marked at the point of maximal tenderness in the holding area. A 1.5-cm longitudinal incision was made directly over the preoperative marking. A mildly protuberant, vascular mass was immediately identified. panels.figure_caption: Intra-nuclear inclusion bodies of glomus tumor cells. A H&E stain under 600x magnification demonstrates intranuclear inclusions marked by the black arrows within the glomus cells, a feature occasionally observed in these tumors. The inclusions appear as eosinophilic or clear structures within the nuclei, causing nuclear enlargement and irregularity. These findings, along with the characteristic round glomus cells and perivascular arrangement, support the diagnosis of a glomangioma.

source_variant.figure_caption: Histopathological and immunohistochemical features of gastric glomangioma. (a) Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E, ×40): a submucosal proliferative tumor lesion composed of small clusters of glomus cells surrounding dilated, erythrocyte-filled vessels (*), resembling cavernous hemangioma-like structures. (b) H&E (×100): the tumor consists of uniform, small, round glomus cells with monotonous round nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and amphophilic to lightly eosinophilic cytoplasm. These cells exhibited sharply defined borders (→) and were arranged in clusters surrounding dilated vascular structures (*). (c) Smooth muscle actin {SMA} immunohistochemistry {IHC} (×100): diffuse SMA positivity, consistent with glomus tumor phenotype. (d) Synaptophysin IHC (×100): strong synaptophysin expression, a potential diagnostic pitfall mimicking neuroendocrine tumors.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is axial contrast CT showing expansive polypoid lesion at nasal cavity roof/sphenoethmoidal recess/right posterior ethmoid per caption. Article title Ethmoid glomangioma links lesion to glomuvenous malformation. No vocabulary CT finding matches, so finding captured as proposed only; visceral ethmoid site is atypical for glomuvenous malformation. B: Panel B is second axial contrast CT slice of same expansive contrast-enhancing polypoid lesion originating at confluence of nasal cavity roof, sphenoethmoidal recess, and right posterior ethmoid cell. Same disease attribution to ethmoid glomangioma from title plus captioned manifestation; no vocabulary CT term, so proposed finding only; atypical visceral location.
